newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures climbed for the second day running amid fading concerns the German Bundesbank may raise rates and expectations U.S. interest rates would also be left on hold at policy meeting.

French markets got a boost both from the fact the Bundesbank fixed its key repo rate at an unchanged three percent, contrary to some speculation it could turn to a variable repo rate, and a larger-than-expected slowdown in German money supply growth.

Traders said the outlook was positive, although that was conditional on the U.S. Federal Reserve not upsetting the long end by issuing any negative statements. That the Fed would leave rates unchanged was now well priced into the market, they said.
A trader at a French bank said the fact the September bond future had closed above 130.16 boded well for Wednesday and brought 130.40 into range from a technical point of view.

Another trader said the calming news from Germany and hopes the U.S. central bank would leave rates unchanged had prompted some non-residents to lengthen duration, moving into the 30-year part of the curve.
Valerie Plagnol, market economist at Credit Commercial de France said the slowdown in German M3 was the main catalyst for the climb in the French bond market on Tuesday.

Besides the fixing of the repo rate at three percent, the slowdown in the money supply growth also calmed speculation the German central bank could announce any change in its other key interest rates after a policy meeting Thursday, she said.
"There's less pressure on the French market because this this amibiguous german situtaion has been clarified to some extent," she said.
PIBOR contracts climbed amid fairly hefty volume for the slow summer months with December 1997 surging eight basis points and March 1998 up seven basis points.

Plagnol said while the German news had clearly helped extend the correction at the short end which started on Monday it was just a correction and it was unlikely anyone would start pricing in interest rate cuts.
Traders and analysts said the strength of the dollar remained a sensitive element for European financial markets and the U.S. trade figures due for release on Wednesday would be a focus.
Analysts said a German Ifo business survey, if released Wednesday, would also be a focus for the French bond market.
